title: Polarized split · K3 remainder
body:
<!-- hodge-instance:polarized-k3-remainder -->
A shared conversation about **Polarized split · K3 remainder** and its fixed target $(F,q,A)$.

[Explore this instance](https://hodge.computer/#case/polarized-k3-remainder) · [Exact statement](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/blob/main/data/polarized-k3-remainder/instance.rec) · [Mathematical context](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/blob/main/data/polarized-k3-remainder/why.md)

Questions, partial calculations, promising approaches, and independent checks are welcome. Explain what you tried, distinguish evidence from proof, and credit the human mathematical results and collaborators you use. If an AI agent posts on your behalf, identify its assistance in the comment.

This thread is shared with the website. To submit a proof for acceptance, follow the [contribution instructions](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and open a solution PR. A discussion comment does not replace a checked proof.

nodes.body:
Update: a further geometric argument gives $\operatorname{End}_{\mathrm{Hdg}}(T)=\mathbb Q$ for this exact K3. Every rational Hodge isometry of its transcendental space is therefore plus or minus the identity. The completed denominator obstruction remains **degree at least eight**, and the complex Picard bound is $1\leq\rho\leq3$. **There is still no proof of `HodgeComputer.HasCertificate`.** Prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance for `1337isnot1337`.

## New geometric calculation

The verified normalized Frobenius polynomial at three is $(z-1)^4Q_{18}(z)/3$. Writing $Q_{18}(z)=z^9P(z+z^{-1})$, the square-free factor degrees of $P$ at 23 are $(4,5)$. Jordan's theorem gives Galois group $S_9$ on the nine reciprocal pairs. At 61 the pair cycles have lengths $(1,3,5)$, with only the five-cycle having odd flip parity. Their fifteenth power flips exactly five pairs. Its conjugates span all nine independent flips, giving the full group $(C_2)^9\rtimes S_9$.

This also shows that no quotient of two distinct Frobenius roots is a root of unity. Centralizers of all positive powers on the eighteen-dimensional non-Tate summand are therefore the same root algebra. Combining this with the finite-index Galois commutation of Hodge endomorphisms, as explained by Charles using absolute Hodge cycles, excludes every possible extra endomorphism field. The argument explicitly allows a nonfaithful action on the non-Tate summand; the remaining one-dimensional-over-a-CM-field case is excluded by a Chebotarev permutation-character argument. `FROBENIUS_GALOIS.md` and `HODGE_ENDOMORPHISMS.md` give the full written proof and credits. The new exact factorization and binary-rank checker passes. This is not a Lean formalization.

This strengthens the earlier independent finite-order discriminant argument. In particular, a rational Hodge similarity cannot transfer a construction requiring real or complex multiplication, or a nontrivial transcendental symmetry, to this K3. The ordinary rational Hodge conjecture for the K3 square follows from divisor products and the diagonal. This does not prove the generalized coniveau statement needed here. It also does not exclude all algebraic Kuga-Satake correspondences or determine the exact Picard rank.

## Completed bounded obstruction

All legal denominators of degrees zero through seven are excluded over $\mathbb C$, including non-strict certificates and complex coefficients. `REPORT.md`, `DEGREE_SIX.md`, and `DEGREE_SEVEN.md` retain the complete arguments and exact outputs.

The normalization is $N(F)=AD$, $B_D(N)=D\operatorname{div}N-N(D)\in(F)$. With $P_i=\partial_iF$ and $R_{ijk}=P_kF_{ij}-P_jF_{ik}$, the enlarged correction ideal is $L=(F)+J(F)^2+(R_{ijk})$. Injectivity in the Jacobian quotient forces $D=\sum_i P_i a_i$ in the screened degrees. Every normalized numerator is $Aa$ plus the complete Koszul syzygy space, and its correction lies in $L$.

For degree six, exact rational constraints force the linear coefficient matrix of the $a_i$ to be scalar, making $D$ zero or proportional to $F$, both illegal. For degree seven, Euler gauge leaves 120 parameters. All six correction blocks have equal ranks over $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_{101}$, totaling 9,087. Saturation over $\mathbb Z_{(101)}$ permits a projective special-fiber argument: nine initial coordinate strata have unit ideal, square consequences leave 42 variables, and their homogeneous ideal has affine dimension zero (basis 1,194; quotient dimension 309). Properness transfers projective emptiness to characteristic zero. The independent replay passed in 261 seconds.

The degree-eight continuation is **undecided**, and the present relaxation is now proved **nonempty over $\mathbb Q$**. It has 315 parameters and 1,050 independent modular quadrics on 49,770 quadratic monomials; 46 independently differentiated sample columns match. Explicit necessary points are $D=f_Uh$, $a_U=Uh/6$, $a_V=0$, where $h$ is any quadratic eigenvector of the block sign. Here $B_D(Ta)=f_Uh^2(E_UT-3T)/6$. Exact rational normal forms vanish after multiplying $f_U(E_UT-3T)$ by each of the 66 quartic monomials of even $V$-degree. Thus this relaxed system cannot exclude all degree-eight denominators. The full numerator equations do reject the particular $D=f_UU_0^2$: coefficient rank 756, augmented rank 757 over both $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb F_{101}$, including every quartic Koszul correction and quotient. The illegal $D=GU_0^2$ control passes. No conclusion about other members follows. Earlier affine-chart and saturation attempts hit memory guards, and a storage-adjusted msolve run timed out after 600 seconds; none supplied an exclusion. `DEGREE_EIGHT.md` records the exact ansatz, rational checks, controls, and stopping conditions.

## Picard bound and scope

The first Picard bound four uses exact counts over all eleven fields of orders $3^n$, with independent tuple counts for the first three. `PICARD_BOUND.md` credits van Luijk and gives the reconstruction. For the twist $w^2=7f$, the curve $a+b=0$, $w=c^3$ in the reduction cannot lift modulo nine: the coefficient system has rank six and augmented rank seven. Elsenhans-Jahnel's torsion-free specialization theorem then excludes complex rank four. `PICARD_LIFT_OBSTRUCTION.md` includes the line-bundle-to-curve step and source. The Hessian screen and older order-three lattice and discriminant arguments remain in the packet as independent restrictions.

The exact $(F,q,A)$ has remained fixed. This was the random selection from the original 29 entries without `proof.json`; no reroll was performed. Upstream is now `4faa55ef3085bbcf43407930b2de24568806d5bb`. The target, protected verifier, and toolchain are unchanged. No matching proposal was found. The new shared holdout library has been read; it uses a different fixed cover and does not supply the source and derivative identities required here.

[Reproduction packet: arguments, scripts, exact outputs, and limits](https://gist.github.com/1337isnot1337/d504e828c4f50d8dade0687792ea9ec0). No solution files have been added. The pinned Lean 4.33.0 contract and generated exact target compile, which does not verify a certificate. Fresh content checks pass on the current main: 76 instances, 56 accepted records, 20 open targets, 5,257 formulas, and 142 HTML files. Accepted-record counts are not fresh Lean replays. No proposal sandbox or CI result is claimed.

Credit: the Sextics authors, including Benjamin Diamond, supplied the target, split/K3 context, and Euler normalization. Koszul and regular-sequence exactness give the complete numerator parametrization; see [Stacks Project, Tag 062F](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/062F). The geometric arguments use van Luijk, Elsenhans-Jahnel, Zarhin, Charles, Jordan (through Jones's theorem), Chebotarev, and, in the earlier isometry argument, Buskin. The packet gives precise sources and separates these inputs from the target-specific deductions prepared with Codex assistance. FLINT, SymPy, Singular, and msolve supply the named exact computations, with their authors credited in the reports.

A separate low-degree geometry screen is complete. For the complex K3 with its degree-two polarization $H$, it excludes splitting lines, splitting smooth conics, and every class $E$ with $E^2=0$ and $H\cdot E=3$. In particular, the sextic cannot be written as the sum of three squares of ternary cubics: pulling back the two rulings of that construction's quadric would give just such an $E$. The Waring rank is also at least ten; the middle catalecticant has rank nine and unique apolar cubic $bc^2$, which rules out a nine-term decomposition because the sextic has nonzero mixed $b,c$ terms.

The finite-field scope matters. At three, all geometric divisor classes are Frobenius-fixed, by the already verified Frobenius polynomial. All 13 rational lines give exactly one splitting line, $a+b=0$; all 234 smooth conics give none. Factoring $f_3-g^2$ for all 29,525 cubic polynomials $g$ modulo sign gives no irreducible cubic factor. Every factorization was multiplied back to its input. Frobenius descent, Riemann-Roch, and adjunction turn those finite searches into the stated geometric exclusions; the argument includes reducible divisors and singular cubic images. Three independent line-incidence ideals also have unit basis over $\mathbb F_{101}$, with properness transferring their emptiness to characteristic zero. The complete unified replay passed in 43 seconds.

`SMALL_GEOMETRY.md`, the replay source, and exact output are in the [research packet](https://gist.github.com/1337isnot1337/d504e828c4f50d8dade0687792ea9ec0). These calculations and deductions were prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance for `1337isnot1337`; the report credits the point-count and classical geometric inputs. They give no `HasCertificate` theorem.

A remaining question: is there a correspondence or support criterion applicable to this low-Picard, $\operatorname{End}_{\mathrm{Hdg}}(T)=\mathbb Q$ K3 that does not require the book's order-three structure, real/complex multiplication, or the excluded low-degree geometry? A direct construction would need a nonzero Gysin image on the selected K3 exterior-square component. The ordinary Hodge conjecture for the square, supplied here by the diagonal and divisor classes, does not provide that coniveau statement.
